Use these guides to install odin_godot, write compiled Odin scripts, choose a multiplayer framework, and export a game.

Start here#

  • SDK documentation site provides task-based guides for setup, scripting, Kit, Replay, and export, plus system diagrams, an interactive correction lab, examples, and searchable reference.
  • Getting Started: install the Nix toolchain, build the extension, add it to a Godot project, and write + attach your first .odin script (a Node that moves on _process). Continue to the quickstart for multiplayer.
  • The onboarding series collects seven posts for Godot developers coming from GDScript/C#: compiled scripts, struct composition, replicated state, predicted commands, and presentation timing. Read it alongside your first build.

Reference#

  • Authoring Guide: the complete feature reference for writing Odin scripts:
    • the script struct convention (owner first field) and //gd: markers (class / extends / tool / icon / signal)
    • @export: every Variant type, hint tags (range / enum / multiline / file / resource), groups, defaults, getters/setters
    • lifecycle procs, custom methods (@(gd_method)), signals, @(gd_connect), @onready
    • multiplayer RPCs (@(gd_rpc))
    • custom resources, global class names, typed cross-script references, autoloads
    • gd.* helpers grouped by task
    • editor tooling: @tool, gd.is_editor(), custom icons, EditorPlugin
  • Shared API conventions: Odin names, generated prefixes, owner lifetimes, and the normal Kit/Replay frame loops.

Development workflow#

  • Workflow covers building, editing, and debugging scripts:
    • building (build/build_scripts.sh) and the project layout it expects
    • live editing: recompile-and-reload on save, plus the manual script.reload(true) fallback
    • editor support: inline errors (_validate), autocomplete (ols), syntax highlighting
    • debugging: gd.print / gd.error, lldb, reading crash backtraces
    • AOT limitations (no in-editor breakpoints, recompile-on-save latency, …)
  • Debugging expands on Workflow's lldb and crash-backtrace guidance.
  • Pure-Odin Events explains typed one-to-many dispatch through events.Event(T) for scripts in the same dll. It covers direct-call cost, comparison with engine signals and batching, module boundaries, and resubscribing after hot reload.
  • Script Modules describes splitting a large project into res://modules/<name>/ directories, each compiled to its own dll and rebuilt independently on save. It explains full-build and save-time costs, import isolation, communication between modules, reload, collisions, and export. It also covers organization within a single dll through script subpackages, and res://shared/ for types, constants, and pure procedures that several modules may import.

Build multiplayer with Kit#

  • Multiplayer quickstart builds the smallest two-peer session in two source files (examples/hello_net is the maintained copy). The simulation quickstart then moves its fast state to server authority.
  • kit/ overview provides reusable multiplayer game systems (godot:kit/*): sessions, reconnect identity, declarative replication, commands, chat, items, combat, NPC helpers, save/resume, moderation, and transport adapters.
  • kit/sim provides fixed-tick, server-authoritative prediction and reconciliation for contested state. It composes with ordinary session replication on a per-field basis and includes bounded lag-compensation tools.
  • Timelines: choosing a model compares authority and display timing for coop, predict-self, contested-object, and predict-world. Use its worked games and interaction-based selection guide to choose a Kit model.
  • Build a game in a day follows a coop cave crawler from scene setup through Steam invites, using examples/cavecrawl as the reference implementation.
  • Gameplay recipes: the kit + play recipe shows how to compose an entity from play structs and divide a networked behavior into seven responsibilities: State, Cadence, Intent, Authority, Prediction, Reconcile, and Presentation. A worked gun example and five gameplay items show where their fields, commands, and hooks belong.

Learn from the examples#

The experimental Replay library provides a complete-world simulation model alongside Kit. Start with its local Timeline or Godot Session lifecycle; add Party/Room for enrollment and host migration, or P2P for deterministic peer rollback. The starter project uses Session for offline and native server/client play. Replay Loot is the headless model; Hello demonstrates lower-level runners and diagnostics. The support envelope distinguishes implemented policies from deployment and full-game parity claims. Kit and the original games remain independently runnable.

  • examples/cavecrawl is the co-op reference (see kit/): the main Kit packages in one game, covered by a latency-injected, multi-process integration test (run.sh).
  • examples/slopball / examples/slopball3d are small complete Kit games: coop soccer with engine physics through play.Puppet, in 2D and 3D.
  • examples/quickdraw is the server-authority reference (kit/sim): a western duel that exercises lag-compensated hitscan with an A/B acceptance test at 240 ms RTT.
  • examples/speedball uses kit/sim for the same soccer game, with every peer predicting the ball so local touches respond immediately. Compare it with Slopball to see the effect of changing simulation models.
  • examples/survivors is a complete single-player survivors-like in pure Odin with a per-file feature map. Its engine-native host-authoritative coop layer is retained for interop tests.
  • examples/coop_arena is the engine-native peer-authoritative path end-to-end: one codebase, three modes (single-player, native ENet, browser WebRTC with a room-code lobby). It predates the toolkit and shows the raw networking calls that Kit's helpers now coordinate.
  • tests/showcase/ is a minimal pure-Odin coin-collector scene.

Export and distribution#

  • Exporting: native desktop export (the OdinExportPlugin) and web/WASM export (the Emscripten SIDE_MODULE + COOP/COEP serving).
  • Distribution: building the drop-in addon with nix build, cross-compiling the core for Linux/Windows, the consumer install workflow, and the per-platform build and runtime verification status.
  • Publishing is the Godot Asset Library runbook: the release branch (build/release.sh), the submission form values, and consumer-facing quirks.

Design history & internals#

These contributor records describe implementation decisions, earlier development, and the behavior verified at the time:

  • PLAN.md: the original architecture and phased delivery plan.

  • design/script-language-api.md: the ScriptLanguageExtension / ScriptExtension / instance-vtable surface, method by method.

  • design/export-internals.md: how the export plugin compiles + bundles scripts per platform.

  • design/native-boundary.md: the core↔scripts ABI fingerprint, compiler compatibility rule, allocator ownership, and why it adds no dispatch cost.

  • design/web-internals.md: the when WEB split, the five wasm blockers found and fixed, in-browser verification.

  • design/wasm-spike.md: the original Odin → Emscripten SIDE_MODULE proof-of-concept.

  • Replay editor authoring workflow
